cases.statement: One person (P22) in a 26-patient inborn-errors-of-immunity cohort from China carries TNFAIP3 c.2152del; described as heterozygous in the discussion. Sex is given as M in Table 1 but F in supplementary Tables S3 and S4. Onset at 40 months; type 1 diabetes/hyperglycemia, rhinitis, eczema; elevated autoantibodies on antigen microarray.

people.label: P22
people.sex: contradictory: M in Table 1, F in Tables S3 and S4
people.zygosity_or_genotype: heterozygous (stated in discussion for the one TNFAIP3 patient)
people.key_phenotypes: type 1 diabetes / hyperglycemia (onset 40 months); rhinitis; eczema; no recurrent infections; elevated IgG/IgM autoantibodies (incl. IA2) with negative routine autoantibody tests

quotes.quote: | P22 | M | 40 | TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly | Hyperglycemia |  |  |  | Type 1 Diabetes | Rhinitis, Eczema | Anti-infection prophylaxis |
One patient harboring a heterozygous mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene clinically presented with diabetes mellitus but without recurrent infections.

In patient P22, who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, routine evaluation of autoantibodies was also negative, but the results of a microarray revealed significant increases in the levels of several autoantibodies, including those against alpha-actinin, troponin-I, islet antigen 2 (IA2), interferon-alpha1 (IFN-A1), interferon-beta (IFN-B), LPS, La/SSB, and angiotensin II receptor (AGTR).
mutations in IL2RG (P19), CTLA4 (P20–P21), TNFAIP3 (P22), SH2D1A (P23), FAS (P24), DOCK8 (P25), and FOXP3 (P26) were each detected in a single patient

phenotype_specificity.statement: The paper reports immune-mediated diabetes with islet- and inflammation-related autoantibodies; no fever, oral/genital ulcers or other features the paper links to the disease are recorded for P22 in Table 1 (digestive, lymphoproliferative and infection columns are blank). Inclusion required WES-confirmed gene findings, but no statement that other genes or causes were excluded for P22.

quotes.quote: Microarray detected multiple islet‑ and inflammation‑related autoantibodies, supporting immune‑mediated diabetes and a broader inflammation‑associated autoimmunity profile [34–36].

Patients diagnosed with IEIs on the basis of the presence of clinical manifestations, functional test findings and related gene mutations confirmed by whole-exome sequencing were included in our study.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion predicted to cause a frameshift, p.(Arg718GlyfsTer98), from the batch HGVS. The paper states no protein change and no disease mechanism for this variant.

authors_classification.statement: No variant-specific classification. Cohort-level only: the authors describe the cohort's findings as pathogenic mutations across ten genes.

quotes.quote: In this cohort of 26 patients, the majority were male, and a spectrum of pathogenic mutations was identified across ten distinct immunodeficiency-related genes.

concerns: Sex contradiction within the paper: P22 is M in Table 1 but F in supplementary Tables S3 and S4.
No transcript and no protein change stated; c.2152del is mapped to NM_001270508.2 by the pipeline only.

The predicted frameshift p.(Arg718GlyfsTer98) lies near the C-terminus; the panel may wish to check exon position and whether the new reading frame runs past the normal stop (possible escape from nonsense-mediated decay).
Variant appears only in tables and a one-sentence discussion; no case narrative, no Sanger confirmation, no parental testing.
Phenotype (type 1 diabetes with autoantibodies) differs from the classic presentation; the paper does not report the hallmark inflammatory features for this person.
Cohort-level study of 26 IEI patients (Children's Hospital of Fudan University); possible overlap with other Chinese HA20 reports cannot be checked from this paper.
notes_for_panel: Single carrier, table-level report. Age at onset 40 months (Table 1), age 4Y at immunological testing (Tables S3/S4). Raw table row in Table 1 has a merged-cell artefact ('TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly').
